**2 of 4.** Targets `integration/01-arbor-boundary`.

Nucleos moves into this repo at `nucleos/`, alongside `brain/`.

One repo, one bill, one place to work. Nucleos still runs as its own service — "one product" was never "one deployment". `brain/` is already a FastAPI service in this tree with its own `vercel.json`, deployed separately and reached over HTTP; `nucleos/` is the same shape.

**This PR is large because it carries Nucleos's entire history.** Brought across with `git subtree` rather than a squashed copy — this is an audit product, and the provenance of the calculation engine is part of what it sells. The reviewable part is `62ae3d0` (config); everything else is a move.

## What the move earns

Both vendored copies of the contract now live in one tree, so a test compares the schema files byte for byte — the check the two-repo layout explicitly could not do. Both digest checks are kept, since comparing copies wouldn't catch a schema edited on both sides without regenerating.

## The fix phase this carries

Work done in the Nucleos repo before the move, now arriving with it:

| | |
|---|---|
| **F1** | UK CBAM placeholder rates fail closed. The case-list exposure figure is withheld with a reason rather than rendering a number backed by a £45 engineering estimate. |
| **F3** | LlamaIndex removed. `LLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY` and `LlamaParse` have **never appeared in any commit** in that repo's history — no supplier document ever left the infrastructure, so there is no disclosure question. |
| **F4** | Audit chain append-only: deletion becomes a status transition, `verify_chain` separates a documented gap from tampering, and migration 006 revokes DELETE including the default privileges that would restore it. |
| **F5** | Tier collision resolved by renaming. The EU 2023/1773 Art. 4 numbering survives only as a `regulation_tier` citation. |
| **F6** | Default-value mark-up, versioned. **The free allocation schedule was wrong for three years, not one** — 2031/2032/2033 held 38.5/25.5/12.5% against the legislated 39/26.5/14% (Directive 2003/87/EC Art. 10a(1a)). |

## Six extraction defects, all on the live path

Found by building the golden set, all fixed, all pinned:

- **Thousand-separated masses parsed as thousandths.** `24,500.00 kg` read as **24.0** — a 1000× under-declaration, and 24 kg of steel is plausible so nothing downstream caught it. The shared parser also stripped every comma, turning the European `24,5` into 245.
- **Multi-line invoices dropped goods lines.** Claude's lines were merged only when the deterministic layer found *zero*, so a two-line invoice declared half the goods with nothing flagged.
- `origin_country` matched only "origin country", never "country of origin" — the phrasing on invoices and customs Box 34.
- Customs MRN required 20 characters where a real MRN is 18, so none ever matched.
- Mill-cert heat numbers captured the literal word "number".
- Route inference read `Cr` against a dict keyed `CR`, so chromium always read 0.0 — which didn't merely disable the EAF branch but **actively misclassified scrap stainless as BF_BOF**, on a factor table differentiated by route.

## The golden set

17 frozen input/output cases with a deliberate `GOLDEN_UPDATE=1` path. I verified it catches injected regressions rather than merely passing. It covers the live extraction path, all four previously untested parsers, method selection, the mark-up table, the Art. 10a(1a) schedule and the HMRC return.

**It has passed unchanged through every phase since.**

## Phases 2 and 3

Nucleos becomes text-in only: every browser-facing upload endpoint, the document-to-text extractor, PaddleOCR and the background pipeline are deleted (RISKS #10 removed rather than wrapped).

Deleting the pipeline broke something the plan didn't anticipate: evidence atoms reached a case *only* through document ingestion, so the report package's audit block and explain-by-field would have gone **empty rather than failed** — an audit trail that stops working while still returning 200. Arbor produces the evidence now, so the JSON draft contract carries it.

Phase 3 splits `cpr_calculator` so it needs no database, adds `POST /internal/calculate` (synchronous, fails closed), and ships versioned CPR reference data.

1047 Python tests pass, golden set green.
